_meta.description: Document-rules config for divorce_hma — contested divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Vishal/Priya may not modify legal grounds or citations.

title: Petition for Divorce under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955

fields.label: Date of separation / cessation of cohabitation
Narrative of facts grounding the petition
Particulars of adultery (named co-respondent if any)
Express denial of collusion / connivance (S.23 HMA)

mandatory_clauses.name: Valid Hindu Marriage
mandatory_clauses.description: Pleading that marriage was solemnised per Hindu rites and parties are Hindus within S.2 HMA

mandatory_clauses.name: Cohabitation History
mandatory_clauses.description: Place(s) where parties resided together as husband and wife

mandatory_clauses.name: Statutory Grounds u/s 13 HMA
mandatory_clauses.description: Specific grounds invoked with particulars — cruelty / desertion / adultery / etc.

mandatory_clauses.name: No Collusion or Connivance
mandatory_clauses.description: S.23(1)(a) HMA — express averment that petition is not presented in collusion

mandatory_clauses.name: No Condonation
mandatory_clauses.description: S.23(1)(b) HMA — petitioner has not condoned the matrimonial offence

mandatory_clauses.name: No Improper or Unnecessary Delay
mandatory_clauses.description: S.23(1)(d) HMA — explanation of any delay in filing

mandatory_clauses.name: Prayer Clause
mandatory_clauses.description: Prayer for dissolution of marriage by decree of divorce

mandatory_clauses.name: Advocate Responsibility Disclaimer
mandatory_clauses.description: Standard Lawie disclaimer — advocate retains responsibility for accuracy

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {petitioner_name}, aged about {petitioner_age} years, resident of {petitioner_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above petition are true and correct to the best of my knowledge derived from records and personal experience, and paragraphs relating to legal submissions are believed to be true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Petitioner

promptInstructions: Draft a contested divorce petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
Open with valid Hindu marriage averments — date, place, ceremonies (saptapadi / kanyadaan), both parties Hindu within S.2 HMA.
Plead matrimonial home(s), children of marriage, and date of separation.
Set out the specific S.13 ground(s) selected with cogent particulars. Avoid vague allegations.
For CRUELTY: Cite Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli (2006) 4 SCC 558 and Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh (2007) 4 SCC 511. Mental and physical cruelty both pleadable.
For DESERTION: Plead continuous period of two years immediately before petition, with animus deserendi. Reference Bipin Chandra Jaisinghbhai Shah v. Prabhavati (1957) AIR SC 176.
For ADULTERY: Plead specific instances; co-respondent may be named (Rule 7 HMA Rules state-specific).
Include mandatory S.23(1) averments: no collusion, no condonation, no improper delay, no taking advantage of own wrong.
Establish jurisdiction under S.19 HMA — marriage solemnised within / respondent resides within / parties last resided together within / petitioner resides within (where respondent is outside India).
Use formal, respectful language. Address court as 'this Hon'ble Court'.
Do NOT generate verification block or advocate signature — added programmatically.
Append Lawie disclaimer: 'Lawie is a drafting assistant. The advocate is responsible for legal accuracy and filing.'

sections.description: Grounds for divorce available to either spouse
Adultery — voluntary sexual intercourse with any person other than spouse
Desertion for continuous period of not less than two years
Incurable unsoundness of mind / mental disorder
Virulent and incurable form of leprosy / communicable disease (post-amendment: venereal disease in communicable form)
Renunciation of the world by entering religious order
Presumption of death — not heard of as alive for 7 years
Court to which petition shall be presented — jurisdiction
Decree in proceedings — duties of court (collusion, condonation, delay)

filing_checklist: Marriage certificate / proof of marriage (photographs, invitation card, priest affidavit)
Proof of Hindu identity of both parties
Address proofs of petitioner and respondent
Documents evidencing grounds pleaded (medical records, police complaints, witness affidavits)
Court fee as per state schedule (Bihar / Jharkhand / UP / Delhi vary)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: marriage_date must be before today by at least 1 year (S.14 HMA — bar against divorce within 1 year of marriage, subject to exceptional hardship leave)
grounds_selected must contain at least one S.13 ground
If grounds_selected includes 'desertion_13_1_ib', separation_date must be at least 2 years before filing date
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format (e.g., BCI/State/Year/Number)
key_citations: Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli (2006) 4 SCC 558 — cruelty including mental cruelty; irretrievable breakdown discussed
Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh (2007) 4 SCC 511 — illustrative instances of mental cruelty
Bipin Chandra Jaisinghbhai Shah v. Prabhavati AIR 1957 SC 176 — essentials of desertion: factum + animus deserendi
Dastane v. Dastane (1975) 2 SCC 326 — cruelty standard; preponderance of probabilities
disclaimer: Lawie is a drafting assistant. The advocate is responsible for legal accuracy and filing.
